runs.prompt: What is 17 × 23? Respond with only the integer, no explanation.
Write a detailed step-by-step explanation of how a sliding-window attention KV cache works in transformers, including ring-buffer indexing, for exactly 200 words. Do not stop early.
runs.content:
Sliding-window attention optimizes memory by limiting the KV cache to a fixed window size $W$. Instead of growing linearly with sequence length, the cache stores only the most recent $W$ tokens. When the sequence exceeds $W$, the model must overwrite old entries to make room for new ones.

To implement this efficiently, a ring-buffer indexing system is used. Rather than shifting all existing tensors—which would be computationally expensive—the system maintains a write pointer (index). This pointer tracks the current position in the pre-allocated buffer of size $W$. As new tokens arrive, they are written to `pointer % W`.
